# Manage scopes

You can update or delete org and project scopes after you create them. Common updates include changing a scope's name or description to reflect changes in ownership, environments, or team structure.

If Terraform manages a scope, update or delete that scope in Terraform instead of using the Admin UI or CLI. This keeps your Boundary resources aligned with Terraform state.

<Note>
The `global` scope is always present and you cannot delete it.
</Note>

To update or delete a scope, you need the relevant permissions on that scope. Refer to [Resource tables](/boundary/docs/rbac/resource-table) and [Manage access with roles](/boundary/docs/rbac/manage-roles) for more information.

## Update a scope

You can update an existing org scope or project scope to change its name or description.

Complete the following steps to update a scope:

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Admin console" group="admin">

Select whether you want to update an org scope or a project scope:

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Org">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select **Orgs** in the navigation pane, and then select the org scope you want to update.
1. Select **Org Settings** in the navigation pane.
1. Click **Edit Form**.
1. Update the **Name** or **Description** fields.
1. Click **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Project">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select **Orgs** in the navigation pane, and then select the org scope that contains the project scope.
1. Select the project scope you want to update.
1. Select **Project Settings** in the navigation pane.
1. Click **Edit Form**.
1. Update the **Name** or **Description** fields.
1. Click **Save**.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Run the `scopes update` command and specify the scope ID and the fields you want to change:

   ```shell-session
   $ boundary scopes update \
       -id o_1234567890 \
       -name "operations" \
       -description "Org scope for the operations team"
   ```

1. Confirm that the scope reflects the updated values.

For the full set of supported flags, refer to [`scopes update`](/boundary/docs/commands/scopes/update).

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Use the same workflow for org scopes and project scopes. The following example shows a project scope.

1. Update the `boundary_scope` resource in your Terraform configuration.

   ```hcl
   resource "boundary_scope" "project" {
     name                   = "operations"
     description            = "Project scope for shared operations systems"
     scope_id               = boundary_scope.org.id
     auto_create_admin_role = true
   }
   ```

1. Apply the updated Terraform configuration.

Terraform updates the scope in place.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Delete a scope

Delete a scope when you no longer need the resources grouped under it.

Complete the following steps to delete a scope:

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Admin console" group="admin">

Select whether you want to delete an org scope or a project scope:

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Org">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select **Orgs** in the navigation pane, and then select the org scope you want to delete.
1. Select **Org Settings** in the navigation pane.
1. Click **Manage**, and then select **Delete**.
1. Click **Delete** to confirm.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Project">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select **Orgs** in the navigation pane, and then select the org scope that contains the project scope.
1. Select the project scope you want to delete.
1. Select **Project Settings** in the navigation pane.
1. Click **Manage**, and then select **Delete**.
1. Click **Delete** to confirm.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Run the `scopes delete` command and specify the scope ID:

   ```shell-session
   $ boundary scopes delete -id p_1234567890
   ```

1. Confirm that Boundary no longer lists the scope.

For the full command reference, refer to [`scopes delete`](/boundary/docs/commands/scopes/delete).

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Use the same workflow for org scopes and project scopes. The following example shows a project scope.

1. Remove the `boundary_scope` resource from your Terraform configuration.
1. Apply the updated Terraform configuration.

For example, if your configuration previously defined the following resource, delete that block and reapply:

```hcl
resource "boundary_scope" "project" {
  name                   = "operations"
  description            = "Project scope for shared operations systems"
  scope_id               = boundary_scope.org.id
  auto_create_admin_role = true
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## More information

- To create new scopes, refer to [Create scopes to group resources](/boundary/docs/rbac/create-scopes).
- To learn more about the scope resource, refer to [Scopes](/boundary/docs/domain-model/scopes).
- To learn more about scope commands, refer to the CLI [`scopes`](/boundary/docs/commands/scopes) topic or the API [Scope service](/boundary/api-docs/scope-service) topic.
- To learn more about using Terraform with Boundary scopes, refer to [Terraform patterns for scopes](/boundary/docs/deploy/terraform-patterns/terraform-scopes).
